claims.statement: TermindApp shares its AppModel and persistence container across main WindowGroup scenes, constructing a fresh WindowModel per ordinary/restored scene (or a demo-configured model for a debug screenshot launch without a request ID); RootView holds the model in @State and provides it to environment and focused scene commands, while the external-authentication Window is excluded from ordinary scene-opening commands.

RootView owns one NavigationSplitView and window toolbar, overlays status on the active workspace without docking it, and places Vault, Assistant, Metrics and Settings in front of a persistent workspace deck.

WindowModel separates destination, sidebar mode, page selections/searches, presentation routes and focused workspace state; user sidebar activation can restore Assistant's prior destination, while History is disallowed for focused Telnet/serial sessions.

The persistent workspace deck retains all open workspace views, gates hidden interaction/accessibility, parks hidden layouts at identity-keyed cached usable sizes, and prunes closed IDs rather than relaying every container resize to hidden split trees.

WorkspaceContentView renders stable-ID split leaves and fraction-based branches, previews divider movement locally, keeps a dragged source mounted while omitting it from preview geometry, and disables hidden-workspace shortcut owners.

Vault list and detail children retain identity across the split breakpoint; a covered list keeps its cached size, and detail transitions animate position and reserved space rather than resizing the form.

ManagedCardPage supplies typed sections, stable item IDs, externally owned selection, capabilities and business views to a reusable renderer; drop geometry yields stable-ID mutation intent while resource-specific actions and presentation remain with the page.

The workspace compact Assistant shares a window-local Chat/Archive route with full Assistant but its contextual panel opens conversations without replacing the foreground workspace; transcript and interaction regions receive explicit focused-terminal context, and Escape does not close a conversation when a blocking interaction is present.

TFM transcript owners are cached per window by conversation and surface, preserving native list and presentation state across mounts; the default eight-owner LRU trims unmounted candidates without forcibly evicting mounted surfaces.

ResponsivePageLayoutTests includes visible-window-gated narrow editor cases in English and both Chinese variants, while its offscreen Metrics case verifies native table identity, sorting and scroll retention across width changes.

TFM Welcome projects only this installation's recent connection events and uses their local timestamps, while the History sidebar searches the synchronized all-device timeline and caps displayed matches at 100.
Saved-host SSH, Telnet, and SFTP panes own connection-history events; closing ends the event, moving preserves it, and Serial or unsaved targets are excluded.

TFM History rows resolve each event's sourceDeviceID through the reusable app-wide device directory, so the displayed device name follows directory updates rather than remaining a hostname captured inside the event.

On macOS 26+ the native NavigationSplitView owns the Sidebar background with no extra glass overlay; older systems use an AppKit visual-effect fallback. The mode rail uses one glass capsule with a neutral moving highlight, selected accessibility traits, a key-window focus outline and Reduce Motion-aware animation.

Assistant full-screen and compact surfaces share the window-local selected conversation and Archive flag as a mutually exclusive route; contextual panel Chat, Back and Archive actions keep a workspace in front, whereas full-screen navigation, New Chat menus and explicit expand select the Assistant destination. Closing the last workspace promotes a selected compact Chat or Archive only in Assistant mode, otherwise returning to Vault.

MainWindowCoordinator requests a UUID-valued main scene for moving a workspace and leaves the live workspace in the source until the native destination registers; registration takes and opens the same workspace in the destination model rather than closing and reopening its session.

Closing a registered main window unregisters its model and calls closeForWindow, which disconnects all workspaces and clears window-local reopen, drag, route and transcript cache state; a restored window without a pending request retains its system-restored frame.

The Navigator's workspace inline rename starts with the full localized displayed title before the native field receives focus; commits delegate to WindowModel, which rejects unrenameable workspaces, trims names and stores split-workspace names on the group but single-pane names on the pane.

The Navigator overlays an AppKit-compatible workspace layout drop receiver above native List rows; it uses live window drag state and measured row frames to preview insertion, excluding the dragged workspace when calculating its mutation index, then reorders a workspace or detaches a pane only on a valid drop in Navigator mode.

Workspace row drag state starts on macOS 26 only after the native List drag session becomes active, while older systems set it in onDrag; the model documents that an older release outside a destination can leave stale drag state until the next click/drag, so drop callbacks validate the pasteboard.

Workspace Navigator expansion is a persisted presentation preference, independently of workspace ownership: selecting a Vault or workspace destination expands its section, and its row menu routes selection-sensitive pane actions through the window model.

The Snippets sidebar filters shared host-library snippets with a sidebar-local footer and can insert into a live focused SSH/Telnet terminal; executing a risk-classified snippet requires an additional confirmation. Its persisted package-folding state is distinct from the full Snippets page's expansion.

The History sidebar projects SSH command history, SFTP browse history, or connection history according to the selected workspace's focused pane, while Snippets and History use AppKit ListViewKit-backed rows with separate footer search and blank-area menus rather than changing the titlebar Find target.
Toolbar creation actions derive from the foreground destination rather than the sidebar mode, while Vault Navigator row menus reuse per-page creation verbs even when that page is not in front.

Window Find routing is chosen by the foreground destination and, within a workspace, its focused pane; page queries belong to their page state, Welcome uses its own content search, and a destination without a searchable target offers no toolbar Find.

Find commands target the focused window model, which suppresses pane keyboard claims before activating terminal search and focusing the toolbar control; Welcome redirects focus into its content field and unsearchable destinations do nothing. Toolbar focus ownership is released on explicit user exit so panes may reclaim the keyboard.

On macOS 26+ a background search host contributes system searchable UI without rebuilding the persistent split-view branch; earlier macOS uses an explicit toolbar search field or compact Metrics popover, retaining native field identity and reserving toolbar height even when no Find is offered.

A focused Telnet session resolves to terminal Find and can present search from the command, but the current toolbar findContext terminal branch only binds Serial and SSH sessions, so Telnet has no usable titlebar query binding through that path.

Navigator drop positions within the List receiver clamp to Workspace insertion boundaries rather than requiring the pointer to be inside an individual Workspace row; insertion mutation excludes the dragged workspace.

Workspace tear-off extends the existing List source on macOS 26 and later, configuring failed-drop animation at native willBegin and requesting a new window only for an unaccepted, uncancelled release outside the source frame; Pane titles use a separate native completion source.
Moving a pane to a new window waits for native destination registration; split panes preserve the existing Pane in a new Workspace, while a lone pane moves its original Workspace and name.

The main scene's fresh ordinary WindowModel starts at Vault/Welcome; registration injects shared connections, host and metrics models, history stores and a shared conversation store while each window retains its own workspace and query state.
The main WindowGroup suppresses automatic XCTest windows by default in debug unless TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1, and disables main-scene restoration for tests and screenshot demo launches.

RootView binds native NavigationSplitView visibility to the window's sidebar state and keeps all workspace children in its detail deck while layering the selected non-workspace destination above them; its floating status bar appears only when a workspace is selected.
A persistent window activity bridge reports key-window activity and the focused SSH session's optional remote title independently of whichever pane view is rendering.
Settings routes are window-local and Back climbs the route hierarchy before restoring the previous destination, falling back to Vault when the previous workspace no longer exists.
SettingsPageView cleans up incomplete provider, MCP server and skill drafts on route changes or disappearance, so leaving Settings does not preserve an unfinished editor unconditionally.

WindowModel owns the Vault page and optional work route; opening a page clears the editor route, opening a work route selects its page, and closing work dismisses the route, while VaultWorkDetailView selects a route-keyed resource-specific detail.

VaultWorkEditingSession guards editor-initiated dirty-route transitions with tokened view registrations: a matching dirty route prompts for save, discard or cancel; save proceeds only after successful asynchronous commit, while a failed save cancels the transition and stale editors cannot unregister replacements.

DeviceDirectoryModel invalidates cached names after successful local rename or sync-triggered reload, and reports repository failures through storageError: failed loads yield no directory records, failed renames do not change the current name, and connection-history rows display a dash if the directory cannot resolve an event's device ID.

When the selected combinable workspace is being dragged, WindowModel derives displayedWorkspace as an eligible adjacent merge target without changing selectedWorkspace; RootView activates that deck child and Navigator highlights it, while clearing the drag restores the selected view and no eligible neighbour leaves it displayed.

If scene creation is unavailable a workspace move request does not remove the source workspace; closing the source before destination registration cancels its requests and disconnects its sessions so the late target cannot take a live workspace from it.

On macOS 26+, the background WindowToolbarSearchHost installs a system searchable item only for a findable destination and binds its query to the resolved Find context; dismissing or losing the target releases the toolbar keyboard claim, and Return/Escape invoke context callbacks when available.

WindowModel prevents direct selection of History when the focused pane is Telnet or Serial and reconciles an already-invalid History mode to Snippets; user mode activation also restores the previous destination on returning to Navigator from full Assistant, falling back to Vault if its workspace has closed.

MainWindowCoordinator records ordinary-size and sidebar-width fallback from registered main windows, prioritizing the most recently used window; requested scenes inherit source layout, but restored scenes retain their system frame, and requested full-screen waits for the new window to become key.
Main-window registration disallows AppKit tabbing and establishes full-size transparent titlebar content coordinates before measuring or applying window size.

MainWindowSizeStore validates device-local persisted content size and sidebar width, defaulting to a 1180×740 main size, 320-point visible sidebar when unset; these fallback dimensions do not override individual restored scene frames.

Main-window sizing uses ordinary content coordinates: full-screen requests inherit the source's pre-full-screen size, resize tracking excludes transitions, and the destination enters full-screen only once key; requested frames honor minimum content size and are fitted to the selected screen.

The sidebar width handshake protects a requested width from the split view's initial default measurement; the preferred width changes only after an expected native measurement, and hiding the sidebar preserves its last valid width.

DesignTokens centralizes fixed layout metrics and system-adaptive semantic colors, material/glass and motion modifiers: the sidebar range is 260–520 points with a protected 360-point detail minimum, and sidebar rows draw key/inactive selection styling rather than relying on List selection colors.
The coordinator coalesces repeated requests to move the same workspace or pane from the same source into one pending scene request until destination registration consumes it.
